cues.en: Instructor: In this video, I'm going to tell you about the three measures of central tendency.
cues.zh: 這部影片介紹三個集中趨勢的量。

cues.en: This is really important.
cues.zh: 這非常重要。

cues.en: These three measures of central tendency, the mean, the median, and the mode, fortunately, they all start with the same letter, which happens to be a really great letter of the alphabet,
cues.zh: 也就是mean平均值、median中位數與mode眾數。幸好都以同個字母開頭，恰好是個很棒的字母，

cues.en: I am partial to the letter M.
cues.zh: 我特別喜歡M。

cues.en: Of course, the letter X is also a good letter, but that's for another lecture.
cues.zh: 當然X也不錯，但那是另一堂課的話題。

cues.en: Okay, so let's get started.
cues.zh: 開始吧。

cues.en: What does it mean to be a central tendency?
cues.zh: 集中趨勢是什麼意思？

cues.en: What does this term mean?
cues.zh: 這個術語代表什麼？

cues.en: Well, the central tendency is kind of like the center of gravity in some sense of a distribution.
cues.zh: 某種程度，是分布的重心。

cues.en: If you think about a distribution, the central tendency is the value that you would expect the data points to merge towards.
cues.zh: 想像一個分布，集中趨勢就是預期資料點會聚向的數值。

cues.en: So for the mean, that's actually pretty simple.
cues.zh: 平均值其實很簡單。

cues.en: That's what I'm showing here, the peaks of these different distributions.
cues.zh: 這裡展示的是各分布的峰。

cues.en: In fact, for a Gaussian distribution, all three of these measures of central tendency, the mean, the median, and the mode are all the same thing.
cues.zh: 對高斯分布而言，這三個集中趨勢量，平均值、中位數與眾數，完全相同。

cues.en: Okay, and then this is just a quick note here.
cues.zh: 這裡快速提醒。

cues.en: Central tendency is different from expected value.
cues.zh: 集中趨勢與期望值不同。

cues.en: If you have already heard of this term, expected value, than for now you should just know that central tendency is not the same thing as expected value.
cues.zh: 如果聽過期望值，現在只要知道，它和集中趨勢不同。

cues.en: Under some circumstances, given some assumptions, they can be the same thing, but they are not necessarily the same thing.
cues.zh: 某些情況、某些假設下，可以相同，但不一定。

cues.en: And if you don't know why, or if you don't know what expected value is, then don't worry, I haven't discussed it yet.
cues.zh: 如果不知道原因，或不知道期望值是什麼，不用擔心，還沒介紹。

cues.en: I'm going to have a whole video just about this term in the probability theory section.
cues.zh: 機率理論那一節，有一整部影片談它。

cues.en: For now, I just want you to know that if you've heard of this term, expected value, just note that it's not the same thing as central tendency.
cues.zh: 目前只要知道，如果聽過期望值，留意它與集中趨勢不同。

cues.en: Okay, so let's start with the mean.
cues.zh: 先從平均值開始。

cues.en: That's probably the most commonly used measure of central tendency.
cues.zh: 大概是最常用的集中趨勢量。

cues.en: Here's the formula.
cues.zh: 這是公式。

cues.en: Looks like a lot of terms going on in this formula.
cues.zh: 看起來有很多項。

cues.en: This is all stuff I introduced you to in the section on math prerequisites.
cues.zh: 全都是數學先備知識那一節介紹過的。

cues.en: So the mean is also sometimes called the arithmetic mean.
cues.zh: 平均值有時也叫算術平均數。

cues.en: It's called the arithmetic mean because there's other types of means, for example, there's the geometric mean, and it's also commonly called the average.
cues.zh: 因為還有其他平均，例如幾何平均，也通常稱為average。

cues.en: So the formula is really simple.
cues.zh: 公式非常簡單。

cues.en: You take all of your data values and you sum them up together.
cues.zh: 把所有資料值加總。

cues.en: So you add together all of the data points that you have in your dataset, and then you divide by N, which is the number of data points in your set.
cues.zh: 將資料集的所有資料點加起來，再除以N，也就是資料點數量。

cues.en: Remember that saying N to the power of minus one is the same thing as saying one divided by N.
cues.zh: 記得，N的−1次方，等同1除以N。

cues.en: As far as notation, the mean is commonly indicated either using a horizontal line on top of the letter corresponding to the data.
cues.zh: 記法上，平均值通常用代表資料的字母，上面加水平線表示。

cues.en: So the data set is X and each individual element of the dataset is X sub I, and then X bar would be the mean
cues.zh: 資料集是X，個別元素是x下標i，x bar則是，

cues.en: or the average of the data.
cues.zh: 資料的平均值。

cues.en: And sometimes people use mu, or sometimes people use this mu with a subscript X to indicate that this is the average of the vector X or data X.
cues.zh: 有時用μ，或μ加下標X，表示向量X、資料X的平均。

cues.en: Now, I've already told you before that mu is sometimes used as a population parameter, and sometimes it's more loosely used to indicate sample means as well.
cues.zh: 之前說過，μ有時用於母體參數，有時也寬鬆地表示樣本平均。

cues.en: So sometimes you'll see, you can see these various kinds of notations, so you just have to be mindful of the notation people use.
cues.zh: 所以會看到這些不同記法，要留意人們使用的符號。

cues.en: So the mean is suitable for data that are roughly normally distributed.
cues.zh: 平均值適合大致常態分布的資料。

cues.en: The data don't have to be perfectly normally distributed, they don't have to be perfectly Gaussian distributed, but as long as there's a more or less
cues.zh: 不必完全常態、完全高斯，只要大致，

cues.en: kind of Gaussian-ish distribution, then the mean is going to be an appropriate measure of central tendency.
cues.zh: 有點像高斯，平均值就是適當的集中趨勢量。

cues.en: It is most suitable for interval data and ratio data.
cues.zh: 最適合區間與比率資料。

cues.en: I'm going to discuss whether the mean can and should be used for other data types in a few moments.
cues.zh: 稍後會談，平均值能否、應否用於其他資料類型。

cues.en: Okay, but I wanna start by getting back to this issue.
cues.zh: 但先回到這個問題。

cues.en: So here you see...
cues.zh: 這裡看到……

cues.en: Oh, sorry, actually first we had a a numeric example, and then we get back to the distributions.
cues.zh: 抱歉，其實先有數字例子，再回到分布。

cues.en: Okay, so here's a collection of numbers.
cues.zh: 這是一組數字。

cues.en: This is our dataset X.
cues.zh: 這是資料集X。

cues.en: The question is, what is the average?
cues.zh: 問題是，平均是多少？

cues.en: What is the mean of this dataset?
cues.zh: 這個資料集的平均值是多少？

cues.en: So it turns out that the mean X bar is two.
cues.zh: 結果x bar是2。

cues.en: Now how do we get that from here?
cues.zh: 怎麼算出來？

cues.en: Well, we sum up all of these numbers.
cues.zh: 把所有這些數相加。

cues.en: So we say minus two and four is two, and then one in seven is eight.
So we have two plus eight, and that's 10.
cues.zh: 所以2加8，是10。

cues.en: So the sum of all of these numbers, that's this part here, that is 10.
cues.zh: 所有數的總和，也就是這部分，是10。

cues.en: And then we have to divide by the number of numbers, which is five, and that gives us two.
cues.zh: 再除以數量5，得到2。

cues.en: So that's the average value.
cues.zh: 這就是平均值。

cues.en: Okay, so here you see an example.
cues.zh: 這裡有個例子。

cues.en: Actually, this top one is not the failure scenario.
cues.zh: 其實上面這個不是失敗情況。

cues.en: This is the ideal scenario.
cues.zh: 這是理想情況。

cues.en: This is a Gaussian distribution.
cues.zh: 這是高斯分布。

cues.en: So the mean is going to be the peak of this distribution, the center of this distribution.
cues.zh: 平均值就在峰、分布中心。

cues.en: So you can see that for a Gaussian or more or less kind of roughly Gaussian-ish distribution, the mean is a really great measure of the central tendency of this distribution.
cues.zh: 可見，高斯或大致像高斯的分布，平均值是很好的集中趨勢量。

cues.en: The mean is basically right in the center, and it tells you where you expect to see a lot of data clustering around.
cues.zh: 平均值基本上就在中心，告訴你預期大量資料會聚集在哪裡。

cues.en: Now, let's consider this green distribution.
cues.zh: 現在看綠色分布。

cues.en: It's a bimodal distribution, and it turns out that it has the same mean as this distribution.
cues.zh: 它是雙峰分布，平均值卻和這個分布相同。

cues.en: So the mean of this distribution is here.
cues.zh: 這個分布的平均在這裡。

cues.en: Now, I call this failure in quotes here because it's not a real failure, like dividing by zero would be a real failure, so there's nothing really wrong with this formula.
cues.zh: 我把「失敗」加引號，因為不是真正失敗，像除以0才是，公式本身沒有問題。

cues.en: The problem is in interpreting this result with regards to this distribution and this data value here is actually not a real good measure
cues.zh: 問題是，要對這個分布解讀結果時，這個資料值並不是很好的，

cues.en: of the central tendency of this distribution.
cues.zh: 集中趨勢量。

cues.en: So that's why this is a failure scenario.
cues.zh: 所以這叫失敗情況。

cues.en: We have the mean, but it is not a representative data.
cues.zh: 有平均值，但不具代表性。

cues.en: It's not representative of what the real distribution actually looks like.
cues.zh: 無法代表真正分布的樣子。

cues.en: The conclusion here is you have a distribution that is strongly non-Gaussian, and the mean, although it's sort of mathematically possible to compute,
cues.zh: 結論是，分布明顯不是高斯時，雖然數學上能算平均，

cues.en: it is not a sensible measure.
cues.zh: 卻不是合理的量。

cues.en: It's not a sensible characteristic of a non-Gaussian distribution.
cues.zh: 不是非高斯分布的合理特徵。

cues.en: Here's another example.
cues.zh: 另一個例子。

cues.en: This is a skewed distribution.
cues.zh: 這是偏斜分布。

cues.en: I'll talk about skew more later on, but basically, you know, it has a big lobe over here, but then there's a lot of values that are pulled off to the right here.
cues.zh: 稍後會談偏斜，基本上這裡有個大隆起，但很多值拉向右邊。

cues.en: So there's this big skew off to the right here.
cues.zh: 所以明顯向右偏斜。

cues.en: Now it turns out that the average, the mean of this distribution is right here.
cues.zh: 平均值就在這裡。

cues.en: But when you look at this and someone asks you, just visually point to where most of the data are clustered in this distribution, and your answer is gonna be around here,
cues.zh: 但如果只看圖，有人請你指出大部分資料聚在哪裡，你會說大約這裡，

cues.en: most of the data are clustered around here.
cues.zh: 大多數資料聚在這裡。

cues.en: So you can see that because this is a strongly non-Gaussian distribution, it's really lopsided, then the mean is not a very useful characteristic here.
cues.zh: 這是明顯非高斯、很不對稱的分布，平均在這裡不是很有用的特徵。

cues.en: It's not a real good measure of the central tendency of this distribution.
cues.zh: 不是很好的集中趨勢量。

cues.en: Okay, so here I claim that the mean is suitable for interval numbers and ratio data types.
cues.zh: 這裡說，平均值適合區間數值與比率資料。

cues.en: So interval and ratio data types.
cues.zh: 區間與比率資料。

cues.en: But what about other data types?
cues.zh: 其他資料呢？

cues.en: Let's take a moment and think about this.
cues.zh: 花點時間想想。

cues.en: Is the means suitable for discreet data?
cues.zh: 平均值適合離散資料嗎？

cues.en: Remember, discreet data are data that can only take very specific values, typically integer values.
cues.zh: 記得，離散資料只能取特定值，通常是整數。

cues.en: Well, here's an example.
cues.zh: 舉個例子。

cues.en: The average US family, according to Google, whenever I last looked this up, the average US family has 1.9 children.
cues.zh: 根據Google，在我上次查詢時，美國家庭平均有1.9個孩子。

cues.en: Now, what does that mean to have 1.9 children?
cues.zh: 1.9個孩子是什麼意思？

cues.en: You know, even if you have two children and one of them is missing an arm, you wouldn't call that 0.9 of a person.
cues.zh: 即使有兩個孩子，其中一個少一隻手臂，也不會稱他0.9個人。

cues.en: You would still call that an entire child.
cues.zh: 仍然是完整的孩子。

cues.en: So it doesn't even make sense for 1.9 children.
cues.zh: 所以1.9個孩子，根本沒意義。

cues.en: That's not a sensible number, but that is the average.
cues.zh: 不是合理的數字，但那就是平均。

cues.en: Very often the mean of discreet data can be informative, but you have to interpret it carefully because you can't really interpret it too literally.
cues.zh: 離散資料的平均，經常有資訊價值，但要小心解讀，不能太照字面理解。

cues.en: Now, that doesn't mean that the mean here is wrong, it just means that it's a little awkward and we have to be careful with the interpretation.
cues.zh: 不代表平均值錯，只是有點彆扭，解讀要小心。

cues.en: How about ordinal data?
cues.zh: 次序資料呢？

cues.en: Is the mean suitable for ordinal data?
cues.zh: 平均適合次序資料嗎？

cues.en: I'd like to take a really, really common example, something that you probably use maybe not every day, but possibly once a week in your lifetime.
cues.zh: 用一個非常常見的例子，可能不是每天，但一生中也許每週都會用。

cues.en: You use ordinal data, use the average of ordinal data to help you make decisions.
cues.zh: 使用次序資料的平均，幫忙決策。

cues.en: And an example would be a course rating or a rating of something on Amazon or you know, any website where you're considering buying something or watching something or enrolling in something.
cues.zh: 例如課程評分、Amazon商品評分，或任何考慮購買、觀看、報名的網站評分。

cues.en: So let's say that courses have ratings of one through five quality ratings, and let's imagine that it's whole star ratings only.
cues.zh: 假設課程評等從一到五，而且只允許整顆星。

cues.en: And we say that this particular course, not this course, because this course that you're watching I'm sure would have a much higher rating than 4.3.
cues.zh: 假設某門課，不是這門，因為我相信你正在看的這門，評價會比4.3高很多。

cues.en: I hope anyway.
cues.zh: 至少希望如此。

cues.en: But any given other course would have a rating of 4.3 stars.
cues.zh: 但某門其他課可能是4.3顆星。

cues.en: Now, the reason why this is not quite really appropriate to take the average is that these kinds of ratings,
cues.zh: 取平均不完全適合，是因為這些評分，

cues.en: these are actually ordinal data, and that means that the difference between three stars and four stars is not the same as the difference between four stars and five stars.
cues.zh: 其實是次序資料，三到四顆星的差異，不等於四到五顆星。

cues.en: In other words, 4.3 stars doesn't really mean 30% of the way between four stars and five stars.
cues.zh: 換句話說，4.3顆星，不真正代表從四到五星之間走了30%。

cues.en: Now, does that mean that all of these ratings across everywhere on the commercial side of the internet is all wrong?
cues.zh: 這表示網路上所有商業網站評分，都錯了嗎？

cues.en: No, it just means that it's a little bit awkward, but it's still informative in many cases.
cues.zh: 不是，只是稍微彆扭，但很多時候仍有參考價值。

cues.en: On the other hand, we can imagine other kinds of ordinal data where we probably wouldn't be averaging over.
cues.zh: 另一方面，可以想像其他次序資料，我們大概不會取平均。

cues.en: So if you think about level of education from, let's say a high school degree, a bachelor's degree, a master's degree, and a PhD, you could order those.
cues.zh: 例如教育程度，高中、學士、碩士、博士，可以排序。

cues.en: Let's say, you know, high school is one, bachelor's is two, master's is three, and PhD is four.
cues.zh: 假設高中是1、學士2、碩士3、博士4。

cues.en: So if we just assign those numbers to the different degrees, it would seem a little bit awkward to say that the average degree value in a community is 2.7, right?
cues.zh: 把數字指定給不同學位後，說某社區的平均學歷值是2.7，有點彆扭，對吧？

cues.en: I mean, you could compute that, and it is a little bit informative, you could compare different communities and see if the average is higher, but the reason why that seems awkward
cues.zh: 可以計算，也稍有資訊，能比較社區，看哪裡平均較高。但彆扭的原因，

cues.en: is because the difference between high school degree and bachelor's degree is not the same thing as the difference between a bachelor's degree and a master's degree.
cues.zh: 是高中與學士的差別，不等於學士與碩士的差別。

cues.en: Okay, anyway, so let's go on to nominal data.
cues.zh: 接著看名目資料。

cues.en: Is the mean, the average, suitable for nominal data?
cues.zh: 平均值適合名目資料嗎？

cues.en: Well, the answer here is very clearly no and I will give you one example.
cues.zh: 答案明確是不適合，舉個例子。

cues.en: So let's say we ask people what flavor of ice cream they like, and we will assign the number one to be chocolate, the number two to be vanilla, and the number three to be strawberry.
cues.zh: 詢問冰淇淋喜好，1代表巧克力，2香草，3草莓。

cues.en: So what does it mean to average these preferences, ratings, over a group of people?
cues.zh: 對一群人的這些偏好評分取平均，代表什麼？

cues.en: You could say that the average person likes 1.7 ice cream flavor?
cues.zh: 說一般人喜歡1.7口味的冰淇淋？

cues.en: That doesn't really make sense.
cues.zh: 這沒什麼意義。

cues.en: I mean, it does kind of tell you that most people like vanilla and more people like chocolate than strawberry.
cues.zh: 某種程度，告訴你多數人喜歡香草，喜歡巧克力的人比草莓多。

cues.en: But it's a really awkward way to phrase this, in part because there's no relationship between chocolate being one and vanilla being two.
cues.zh: 但這種表達很彆扭，部分原因是巧克力為1、香草為2之間，沒有關係。

cues.en: We could have also called strawberry number one and vanilla number three and chocolate two.
cues.zh: 也能把草莓叫1、香草3、巧克力2。

cues.en: All right, so the conclusions are that the mean is most appropriate for interval and ratio data.
cues.zh: 結論是，平均值最適合區間與比率資料。

cues.en: The mean for discrete data and ordinal data can be useful in some situations, but it must be interpreted carefully because you can't have 0.9 children
cues.zh: 離散與次序資料的平均，有時有用，但必須小心解讀，因為不能有0.9個孩子，

cues.en: and a rating of 4.5 stars is not necessarily halfway in between four stars and five stars.
cues.zh: 而4.5星，也不一定是四到五星的正中間。

cues.en: And the mean is definitely not appropriate.
cues.zh: 平均值絕對不適合，

cues.en: It's not even sensible for nominal data.
cues.zh: 甚至不適用於名目資料。

cues.en: Okay, enough about the mean.
cues.zh: 平均就說到這裡。

cues.en: In the next video, I'm going to continue talking about the median and the mode.
cues.zh: 下一部影片，繼續談中位數與眾數。
